name: Foundry Local (Windows Foundry)
tagline: Microsoft's official local AI engine and CLI with automatic NPU (Copilot+), DirectML, and CUDA acceleration.
hardwareAcceleration: NPU (Snapdragon X, Intel Core Ultra, AMD Ryzen AI), DirectML, NVIDIA CUDA, CPU (ONNX)

installCommands.macos: brew install microsoft/foundry/foundry-local  # or via pip

pros: Official Microsoft local engine with first-class Windows NPU & DirectML support
Hardware-adaptive execution: automatically maps weights to NPU, GPU, or CPU
Integrated into AnythingLLM, VS Code AI Toolkit, and Semantic Kernel
Built-in OpenAI-compatible background daemon via `foundry service start`
cons: Curated catalog primarily tailored around Microsoft-optimized model checkpoints
Newer tool compared to mature ecosystems like Ollama and llama.cpp
bestFor: Windows 10/11 and Copilot+ PC developers wanting native NPU/DirectML acceleration and Microsoft AI integration.

name: Ollama
tagline: The de facto standard local LLM runner and background daemon with a clean CLI and REST API.
hardwareAcceleration: Apple Metal, NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm

installCommands.macos: brew install ollama  # or download Ollama-darwin.zip
installCommands.windows: winget install Ollama.Ollama  # or download OllamaSetup.exe

pros: Zero-config hardware detection (Metal, CUDA, ROCm auto-enabled)
Background daemon with OpenAI-compatible API on localhost:11434
Massive model library with automated quant pulling
First-class integration with Cursor, Continue.dev, Open WebUI, and LangChain
cons: No built-in chat GUI (requires pairing with terminal or WebUI)
Strict GGUF focus; no native FP8 / AWQ Safetensors support
bestFor: Developers, CLI users, and background services needing a stable local OpenAI API.

name: LM Studio
tagline: All-in-one desktop GUI with built-in Hugging Face model search and local OpenAI server.
hardwareAcceleration: Apple Metal, NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm / DirectML, Vulkan

installCommands.macos: Download from lmstudio.ai (Universal Apple Silicon / Intel .dmg)

quickStart: Launch app -> Search any model from Hugging Face -> Click Download -> Start Chatting or Start Local Server.
pros: Most polished visual UI for searching and downloading models directly from Hugging Face
Intuitive GPU offload slider with live VRAM usage telemetry
One-click local server mode with full OpenAI API compatibility
Supports structured outputs, system prompts, and multiple chat presets
cons: Closed-source core binary
Higher idle RAM overhead than headless CLI engines
bestFor: Users who want a visual, ChatGPT-like desktop experience without touching a terminal.

name: Jan
tagline: 100% open-source, local-first and offline desktop alternative to ChatGPT.

installCommands.macos: brew install --cask jan  # or download .dmg from jan.ai
installCommands.windows: winget install Jan.Jan  # or download .exe installer

quickStart: Open Jan -> Go to Hub -> Download pre-configured models (DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen) -> Chat locally.
pros: 100% open source and privacy-focused; operates completely air-gapped
Built-in Nitro engine (llama.cpp fork) with automatic GPU acceleration
Extensible with community plugins and customizable local API endpoints
Clean, modern minimalist UI
cons: Smaller built-in model hub compared to LM Studio's raw Hugging Face browser
Less granular control over advanced sampling parameters
bestFor: Privacy-conscious individuals and organizations wanting a fully open-source desktop app.

name: Open WebUI
tagline: Feature-rich, self-hosted web UI replicating the full ChatGPT experience with local RAG.

installCommands.macos: docker run -d -p 3000:8080 --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway -v open-webui:/app/backend/data --name open-webui --restart always ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
installCommands.windows: docker run -d -p 3000:8080 --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway -v open-webui:/app/backend/data --name open-webui --restart always ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
installCommands.linux: docker run -d -p 3000:8080 --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway -v open-webui:/app/backend/data --name open-webui --restart always ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main

quickStart: Start container -> Open http://localhost:3000 in browser -> Connects automatically to local Ollama on port 11434.
pros: Full ChatGPT feature parity: multi-user roles, chat history, voice input, markdown & code execution
Built-in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): drop PDFs, spreadsheets, and docs into chat
Web search grounding (Brave, Google, DuckDuckGo) and image generation support
Connects seamlessly to Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, and remote APIs
cons: Requires Docker or Python setup; not a single-click binary
Frontend only; requires an inference engine running in tandem
bestFor: Self-hosters, teams, and families wanting a centralized private web portal for local AI.

name: llama.cpp
tagline: The foundational C/C++ inference engine delivering bare-metal speed across all architectures.
hardwareAcceleration: Apple Metal, NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Vulkan, SYCL, OpenCL, AVX-512

installCommands.macos: brew install llama.cpp  # or git clone and make (Metal enabled by default)
installCommands.windows: Download pre-built release binaries with CUDA or Vulkan from GitHub Releases
installCommands.linux: git clone https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp && cd llama.cpp && cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON && cmake --build build --config Release

pros: Underlying engine behind Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, and KoboldCpp
Zero overhead, minimal dependencies, and maximum hardware control
Industry pioneer of the GGUF specification and k-quants / i-matrix
Includes standalone high-performance server binary (`llama-server`)
cons: CLI-centric configuration with dozens of technical flags
Requires manual management of GGUF shards and context windows
bestFor: Power users and engineers who want maximum throughput, custom compilation flags, and bare-metal control.

name: vLLM
tagline: The enterprise gold standard for high-throughput, multi-user LLM serving with PagedAttention.
hardwareAcceleration: NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Intel Gaudi

installCommands.macos: Not natively supported (Linux / CUDA only; use MLX-LM on macOS)
installCommands.windows: wsl --install  # Run in WSL2 Ubuntu: pip install vllm

pros: PagedAttention virtually eliminates KV cache memory fragmentation
Continuous batching provides up to 10x-24x higher throughput under multi-user concurrency
Native support for Safetensors, AWQ, GPTQ, and FP8 formats
Enterprise production standard compatible with Kubernetes and Ray
cons: Requires Linux or Windows WSL2; no native macOS support
Demands high VRAM and NVIDIA/AMD GPU; not suited for low-memory CPU inference
bestFor: Multi-user production deployments, SaaS backends, and servers with high concurrency requirements.

name: MLX-LM
tagline: Apple's native machine learning framework optimized exclusively for Apple Silicon unified memory.
pros: Fastest possible token generation and prompt processing on M1/M2/M3/M4 Macs
Direct unified memory access eliminates CPU-GPU PCIe transfer bottlenecks
Native 4-bit and 8-bit quantization with built-in LoRA fine-tuning support
OpenAI-compatible server (`mlx_lm.server`) included out of the box
cons: Strictly locked to macOS on Apple Silicon (no Windows or Linux)
Requires Python environment to run
bestFor: MacBook Pro, Mac Studio, and Mac mini owners who want peak native performance on Apple Silicon.

name: AnythingLLM
tagline: All-in-one local desktop and self-hosted app engineered specifically for document RAG.
hardwareAcceleration: Apple Metal, NVIDIA CUDA, CPU (or connects to Ollama/vLLM)

installCommands.linux: Download AppImage or run Docker container

quickStart: Open app -> Choose embedded LLM or connect to Ollama -> Drag and drop PDFs -> Query your knowledge base.
pros: Zero-config local document indexing: drag-and-drop PDFs, Word docs, codebases, audio files
Includes embedded local vector database (LanceDB) and embedding models
Workspace isolation: separate document collections for different projects
Available both as a single-click desktop app and as a multi-user Docker container
cons: Focused primarily on RAG knowledge bases rather than raw model benchmarking
Heavier footprint than dedicated lightweight chat clients
bestFor: Researchers, legal, and engineering professionals needing private, offline document questioning.

name: KoboldCpp
tagline: Single-file executable packing a llama.cpp engine, web interface, and advanced creative samplers.
hardwareAcceleration: NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Vulkan, Apple Metal, CLBlast

installCommands.macos: brew install koboldcpp  # or run python koboldcpp.py
installCommands.windows: Download single koboldcpp.exe from GitHub Releases (no install required)
installCommands.linux: Download koboldcpp-linux-x64 from GitHub Releases and chmod +x

quickStart: Double-click koboldcpp.exe -> Select model -> Browser opens automatically with rich web interface.
pros: Zero installation required: standalone single portable executable on Windows and Linux
Advanced creative sampling parameters: DRY, XTC, Min-P, Mirostat, and grammar constraints
Smart context-shifting prevents prompt reprocessing during long conversations
Exposes both KoboldAI and OpenAI-compatible API endpoints
cons: User interface is retro / utilitarian
Manual model file selection via file dialog
bestFor: Users who want a portable single-file binary with advanced sampling and zero dependencies.

name: Exo
tagline: Distributed P2P cluster engine that stitches disparate Macs, PCs, and laptops into a unified GPU.

installCommands.windows: pip install exo  (requires Python 3.10+ and Git)

quickStart: Run `exo` on machine A and `exo` on machine B on the same Wi-Fi/Thunderbolt network. Devices discover each other automatically.
pros: Runs massive 70B+ or 405B models by distributing layers across multiple consumer machines
Automatic zero-configuration device discovery over local network
Supports heterogeneous hardware (e.g. Mac Studio + Windows PC + Linux laptop)
Exposes a standard OpenAI-compatible API from the primary node
cons: Inference speed is bounded by inter-device network bandwidth (Wi-Fi vs Thunderbolt)
Experimental architecture with ongoing active development
bestFor: Hobbyists with multiple Macs or PCs wanting to pool unified memory to run frontier-scale models.

name: Text Generation WebUI
tagline: The versatile Swiss-Army knife interface supporting multiple backends and fine-tuning.
hardwareAcceleration: NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, CPU

installCommands.windows: Download one-click zip and run start_windows.bat

quickStart: Run start script -> Open http://127.0.0.1:7860 -> Select model loader (llama.cpp, ExLlamaV2, Transformers) -> Load & chat.
pros: Supports nearly every model loader: llama.cpp, ExLlamaV2, Transformers, AutoGPTQ, HQQ
Built-in LoRA training and fine-tuning tab
Extensive extension ecosystem (whisper audio, web search, character cards)
Granular control over raw token generation parameters
cons: Steeper learning curve with complex loader configuration tabs
Large installation footprint with many Python dependencies
bestFor: Enthusiasts who want to experiment with different quant loaders (EXL2, AWQ, GGUF) and local fine-tuning.

name: TabbyAPI
tagline: Lightweight, blazing-fast ExLlamaV2 server tailored for consumer NVIDIA GPUs.

installCommands.linux: git clone https://github.com/theroyallab/tabbyAPI && pip install -r requirements.txt

quickStart: Edit config.yml -> python main.py -> Connect any OpenAI-compatible client to http://127.0.0.1:5000/v1
pros: Fastest generation speed on consumer NVIDIA GPUs using ExLlamaV2 EXL2 weights
Extremely low VRAM overhead compared to generic Hugging Face loaders
Native support for 4-bit KV caching and speculative decoding
Clean OpenAI-compatible endpoints with token-level streaming
cons: Strictly NVIDIA GPU only; no AMD, CPU, or Apple Silicon support
Only supports EXL2 and GPTQ formats (no GGUF)
bestFor: Gamers and developers with NVIDIA RTX 3090/4090/5090 GPUs who want the absolute fastest single-user token throughput.
